newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Oiltanking wins Schiphol jet fuel pipeline tender.
newsitem.headline: Oiltanking wins Schiphol jet fuel pipeline tender.

text.p: An Amsterdam-based oil products storage group, Oiltanking BV, said it has won a tender to feed a planned pipeline to Amsterdam Schiphol airport with kerosene supplies.

A spokesman for German-owned Oiltanking told Reuters that it has won the competition staged by Aircraft Fuel Supply (AFS), a joint venture company co-owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV and 10 multinational oil companies, to supply aviation fuel through a proposed new pipe connection between Amsterdam port and the airport.
The AFS plan to provide airlines at Schiphol with a new pipeline carrying alternative supplies of aviation fuel is currently awaiting approval from local council planners.
The spokesman said AFS has applied to the provincial council of North Holland, and the regional authorities of Haarlem and Amsterdam, for permission to build the proposed pipeline.

Oiltanking BV, which is controlled by the German family-owned holding group Marquard & Bahls, beat off competition from four other oil storage companies which also have facilities in the second biggest Dutch port, he added.
He said specific amounts of kerosene have yet to be negotiated with AFS. However, AFS has said it will require as much as two million tonnes of aviation fuel annually.

AFS, which has been in existence at the airport for some 30 years, has in addition to KLM the following oil companies as shareholders: Mobil, Fina, Chevron, Esso, Kuwait Oil Company, Elf, Total, British Petroleum, Texaco and Shell. Each of the 11 companies has a 9.09 percent share in the venture.
